recaps.ending:
Jason ends the Builder's immediate campaign by returning the unstable authority token. In exchange, the Builder withdraws its forces from Pallimustus and promises one future opening to the fundamental realm, which Jason needs to anchor a bridge to Earth. Jason survives the mine-rescue portal disaster and continues recovering, but his transformed soul space is now a secure astral domain in which he has immense control. Using that power outside remains dangerous at silver rank.

Melody Jane remains confined in Jason's pagoda. She is Sophie's mother, and neither Jason nor Carlos yet knows how to reverse her altered lesser-vampire condition without killing her. Sendira's two stolen clockwork kings, the Order's mass messenger summonings, and the false power behind Purity remain open threats. Dawn leaves Pallimustus after warning Jason to prepare rapidly for a future crisis. Farrah remains his ally but departs the adventuring team to establish a government-backed communications venture with Travis. Rufus stays temporarily to train Jason as the group prepares to leave Rimaros and travel toward Greenstone. The Earth bridge, messenger dimensional knowledge, and the Builder's artificial-world project remain unfinished.
recaps.in_short: During the weakened Storm Kingdom's monster surge, Jason Asano and his allies uncover the Order of Redeeming Light's scheme to convert essence users and build a construct army with stolen Builder technology. The team captures Order leader Melody Jane, revealed as Sophie's mother, and Belinda cripples the Order's mountain refuge. Jason nearly dies forcing civilians out of a flooded mine, and the disaster transforms his soul space into a nascent astral domain. He later bargains away unstable Builder authority in exchange for the Builder's worldwide withdrawal and one future opening to the fundamental realm needed for the bridge to Earth. Dawn teaches him the limits of his new status as an astral king, then departs with a warning about a future crisis. Farrah leaves field work to build a communications network with Travis, while Rufus stays to train Jason. The stolen clockwork kings, converted prisoners, messenger forces, Earth bridge, and Builder's larger design remain unresolved.

recaps.text: Previously: Jason Asano, an outworlder from Earth, returned to Pallimustus carrying the effects of conflicts that had changed both his body and soul. He rejoined Farrah Hurin and his adventuring circle as a silver-ranker with unusual aura, portal, and spirit-domain powers. His past involvement with the Builder made him central to the continuing astral crisis, while his experiences on Earth left him wary of accepting responsibility for every threat beyond his rank. The earlier fighting against the Builder devastated forces around the Sea of Storms and killed Vesper Rimaros during the battle over a flying city. The Builder's withdrawal from that immediate conflict did not end the monster surge or repair the region's losses. Jason also retained a long-term objective beyond the current campaign: preserving the connection between Earth and Pallimustus.

Jason's team begins with monster-clearance contracts in the weakened Storm Kingdom, where postwar losses have left surge zones short of adventurers. At a fortress town, three teams find a civilian massacre, a lone survivor, missing essence-user bodies, and defences deliberately drained by insiders. The clues point toward the Order of Redeeming Light, an extremist Purity faction that changes people into human-presenting adherents.

Liara Rimaros then leads six teams into a fallen Builder city to search for an active construct factory. Newer constructs appear adapted to Jason's abilities, and the ruins prove to be a full-scale model rather than a genuinely inhabited city. The expedition is interrupted when Order forces arrive by concealed underwater transports. Their modified clockwork cores strip essence users of their original powers and turn them into controlled servitors. The Order has been creating shortages at remote fortress towns, converting defenders, removing them during attacks, and leaving civilians to die behind sabotaged shields. Its immediate objective is to steal clockwork kings and produce more cores. Melody Jane commands the local operation, with Sendira leading one of the landing groups.

The expedition fights Order forces across Builder Island while a false-aura beacon blocks tracking, portals, and long-range movement. Jason's afflictions, Sophie's mobility, Clive's battlefield control, and the combined teams break one enemy group and secure prisoners, but other Order members escape with captive adventurers. Jason contains the beacon inside his spirit realm, where it is dismantled without the disastrous backlash expected from disabling it normally.

With tracking restored, Jason rescues one prisoner and sends Shade to follow the captors. The larger theft still succeeds: Sendira finds an operating underground factory, controls two intact gold-rank clockwork kings, and extracts them through a remote portal supplied by Esteban Gallo. The Order also abducts Gibson Amuz. He is not merely another adventurer but the heir to a mining house controlling extensive resources around the Sea of Storms. Melody uses that revelation to defeat an internal challenge from rival cell leaders. Her plan is to force mining knowledge from Gibson, fund an independent construct facility, and use the stolen kings to manufacture armies rather than depend solely on converted followers.

Liara investigates the concealed Order base and the corrupted gold-rank portal network while Shade's infiltrating bodies remain unable to report. Jason's companions take surge assignments near Rimaros. On a solo delivery, Sophie escapes a hidden gold-rank sea monster through sustained speed and dimensional movement, causing one of her racial gifts to evolve. She later defeats hired gang members who knew her route and learns they were employed through Purity loyalists, although Jason and Liara recognize the offered lead as a likely trap.

Liara's frustration over Gibson's capture leads her to seek Jason's advice. He urges disciplined investigation rather than anger-driven retaliation, drawing on his experience with a hidden organization on Earth. Their working relationship becomes more trusting, and Liara narrows the Builder Island extraction to falsified records involving a remote gold-rank portal user. The anti-Builder office expands into the Office of Organised Enemy Response and adds Purity to its remit. A gold-rank visitor then offers information about Sophie's missing mother while withholding his own purpose. Sophie wants the information but rejects his terms. Vidal Ladiv is assigned to debrief her and discovers that Jason's entire team is treated as unusually sensitive by the Adventure Society.

The Order raids the Amuz mining complex for materials needed by its construct project. Deep granite blocks ordinary portals and communications, forcing Liara's rescue force to enter through the dock. Baseph Rimaros, Liara's husband, tries to protect mine workers by activating destructive final defences. Jason's team secures the insertion point and advances through the tunnels while Vidal guides evacuations.

Immediately before deployment, Sophie learns that Melody Jane, the Order's leader, is her mother. Baseph's sabotage seals and floods sections of the mine, separating the rescue teams and killing some people outside safe rooms. Jason is trapped with Melody and fights her until Sophie and the others breach the barrier. Sophie helps suppress and capture her mother alive. Elsewhere, Order forces escape with supplies and assistance from an adventurer team that betrays the dock defenders. Jason's group rescues the guilt-stricken Baseph, but becomes confined in a safe room with civilians, Melody, and a gold-rank converted force approaching. The converted are understood as victims whose bodies are controlled while their souls remain intact, leaving the team obligated to resist them despite the coercion.

With the mine safe room under attack, Jason draws on an exceptionally powerful energy reserve and forces an unsafe portal through the deep granite. He evacuates his team, Baseph, Melody, and the civilians into his cloud construct, but the effort catastrophically overloads his body and soul. Colin replaces ruined portions of his body, Gordon forms an unexplained ritual, and Clive and Neil help contain the excess mana. The cloud house becomes a black temple-like domain that attacks untrusted entrants. Carlos Quilido determines that Jason will survive, although recovery may take weeks.

While Jason remains unconscious, Belinda infiltrates the Order's mountain stronghold with Shade hidden in her shadow. Liara had deliberately allowed known traitors to flee the mine along a monitored route, revealing the refuge. Belinda sabotages its locks, utilities, vessels, and underwater exit, then activates a beacon for Liara's assault force. Trenchant Moore breaches the mountain as the attack begins. Belinda escapes in the last usable submersible with a captured converter, while Gibson is left for specialists to remove from an active ritual. Melody remains securely confined by autonomous avatars inside Jason's transformed domain, and Dawn stays nearby until Jason wakes.

Jason's recovery reveals the scale of the portal disaster. His altered physical-spiritual gestalt survived only through his familiars, domain, and the team's intervention. The Order's purification proves to be a modified lesser-vampire curse, and its supposed God of Purity may be an impostor because forced conversion contradicts Purity's nature. The church has also completed mass messenger summonings. Carlos presses Jason to aid that wider fight, triggering a dangerous outburst before Arabelle helps Carlos recognize the harm he caused.

Jason's soul consumed the old bridge artifacts and formed an Astral Gate, an Astral Throne, a bridge anchor, and a volatile Builder authority token. The bridge to Earth can still be built, but Jason now needs messenger dimensional theory and access to the fundamental realm. Shako arrives as the Builder's vessel to reclaim the token, only for it to reject him. Jason forces direct negotiations with the Builder and World Phoenix through Shako and Dawn. He returns the authority in exchange for the Builder's immediate worldwide withdrawal and a promised one-time opening to the fundamental realm. The bargain ends the local Builder campaign, although the Builder's withheld message and the World Phoenix's concealed future concern remain unresolved.

The Builder's forces withdraw across Pallimustus, and Jason's companions return from surge work to support him. Public knowledge of his dealings with transcendent beings draws attention from royal, aristocratic, Adventure Society, and Magic Society interests. Jason explains that his spirit domains are stable expressions of authority, while the transformed Cloudflask and Reality Hegemon title carry powers that could destroy him if mishandled. He rejects attempts to treat that authority as a prize others may control.

Carlos apologizes for putting his anti-messenger cause ahead of Jason's welfare and resumes treating him. His research confirms that completed Order transformations cannot simply be cleansed without killing their subjects, leaving Melody confined and any cure a long-term project. Jason also makes Liara return with Baseph before granting an official audience, establishing that the royal family must negotiate rather than command him. Soramir Rimaros supports that cautious approach because Jason may eventually become a diamond-ranker. Once Carlos clears dimensional activity, Rufus begins training Jason in combat trances. Jason tests his changed portal powers and enters his transformed soul space through a new Cloudflask gate. Dawn identifies it as a nascent astral domain: Jason is now an astral king.

Inside his astral domain, Jason learns that the Astral Throne gives him near-total control over matter and energy within his own soul space, but only sharply limited authority outside it. He cannot safely rewrite another person's soul, and using the throne or Astral Gate to amplify himself at silver rank would produce severe backlash. A possible cure for Melody would require Jason and Carlos to understand the original transformation well enough to replace it without a lethal transition.

Dawn reveals that the Builder is assembling an artificial world from plundered astral spaces, apparently seeking the kind of embodiment Jason naturally has with his domain. She then leaves Pallimustus after warning Jason that a future crisis will require him to become stronger as quickly as possible. The Builder has withdrawn under Jason's bargain, but its larger project and message remain open. The Order has lost its mountain refuge, yet Sendira's stolen clockwork kings, the messenger summonings, and the false Purity power remain unresolved. Farrah leaves field adventuring to establish a government-backed magitech communications network with Travis. Rufus stays with Jason's team for the journey toward Greenstone, training Jason in swordsmanship and combat trances while Jason continues his recovery and prepares for the unfinished bridge to Earth.

recaps.ending: Yoresh survives the messenger raid, while the Garuda contains the Naga Genesis disaster in the city centre. Jason's deep-astral ritual breaks the invaders' linked aura advantage, and the messenger command ultimately withdraws. Jason defeats Terra June Castor but refuses to kill her. He removes the astral-king brand and seal that bound her, then grants asylum in his astral realm to Terra, a gold-rank messenger commander, the commander's companion, and other defectors. He helps consenting messengers replace their former ruler's marks without making them his slaves, proving their dependence on astral kings can be broken. One messenger dies when the former astral king withdraws its mark before consent can be given. The intervention alerts that astral king and prompts a council. The defectors disagree over concealment and open revolt. An unknown objective beneath a dangerous natural array, a subterranean city, an astral space, and Builder cultists becomes the next likely mission. Purity's core-cleansing relic, regional worm risks, Melody's condition, and the route back to Earth all remain unresolved.
recaps.in_short: Recovering from a near-fatal rescue, Jason Asano leaves Rimaros under a false identity and travels with his team while Amos Pensinata trains his aura control. A messenger trail leads the convoy to Yoresh, where a network of world-taker worms has killed whole settlements. The team destroys a breeding site, rescues prisoners, and turns Jason's cloud construct into a refugee hospital and bunker. A Naga Genesis threat erupts as messengers besiege the city. Jason breaks their linked aura suppression with a deep-astral ritual, exposing himself as an alternative to conventional astral-king rule. After sparing Terra June Castor, he removes her binding mark and shelters messenger defectors, later freeing those who consent without enslaving them. Yoresh survives, but Jason's act alerts an astral king. The defectors reveal a deeper campaign around a dangerous natural array and an unknown buried objective, while the searches for Purity's core-cleansing relic and a path to Earth remain open.

recaps.text: Previously: Jason Asano returned from Earth carrying deep trauma and powers that no longer fit ordinary rank expectations. His soul had become a physical astral realm, and his relationships with great astral forces made him both valuable and dangerous to established powers. Farrah Hurin had been revived and shared an unusual residual bond with him. Jason's allies had helped destroy the Builder's flying city, while the Order of Redeeming Light had transformed captives through forced purification. The aftermath left Melody Jane in Jason's custody and Gibson Amouz in specialised care. Rimaros also carried recent losses, including Vesper Rimaros, and Jason's public power had made him a political problem as well as an adventurer. He still hoped to create a bridge back to Earth, but lacked the messenger astral knowledge needed to complete it.

Jason remains in prolonged recovery after a portal rescue nearly killed him and broadcast his aura across Rimaros. His cloud house has changed with his soul, becoming a stronger refuge that unsettles even experienced allies. The Adventure Society and royal representatives propose a public separation from his team, followed by his return under a discreet auxiliary identity. Jason accepts the outline and begins assembling support personnel who can make the cover credible. Meanwhile, an information broker identifies the man responsible for Jason's forced starseed implantation and links him to the Order of Redeeming Light's portal specialist. When the broker is abducted as bait, Jason's allies recognise the trap and arrive with overwhelming support. They rescue the broker and capture the starseed implanter alive. The captive may know the portal specialist's identity, but Jason has not yet decided how to handle him. Jason's recovery, dangerous Astral Gate use, and unwanted prominence also remain unresolved.

Dawn's real auxiliary plan adds trainers, researchers, and a scout to Jason's proposed cover, while Jason refuses to turn his soul space into a prison for Order captives. A group of adventurers then targets a familiar-binding ritual to challenge him. The ritual is moved to safety, and Jason methodically isolates and captures the hunters without killing them. Their Adventure Society standing is likely ruined. Autumn successfully binds a giant frog-like hydra. At the same time, Jason's group prepares for a royal celebration ball intended to reassure Rimaros's political class. Liara Rimaros warns that rival houses may provoke a duel through lesser allies. Jason enters the event expecting manipulation, while Zara Rimaros discusses the royal family's desire to place a representative in his travelling group. Jason refuses to decide until the proposal is handled openly within the family. The party arrives at the ball prepared for the expected political provocation.

The ballroom provocation becomes a series of real duels. Jason first forces an inexperienced challenger to retreat by insisting that any contest carry genuine consequences. A more credible relative then offers cloud-flask materials and vehicle designs as stakes. Soramir Rimaros reopens an old arena, and Jason selects Rufus, Sophie, and Humphrey to fight beside him. Before the matches conclude, four hired gold-rank core users infiltrate Jason's pagoda and use an illegal device that destroys a large part of the structure. Its defences trap and continually injure them. Farrah confronts Jason over the cruelty of his response and helps him recognise the violent habits he brought back from Earth. In the arena, Sophie, Rufus, and Humphrey win their contests. Jason ends his own duel almost immediately with a precise soul attack, forcing Soramir to intervene. The public display confirms that Jason cannot be handled like an ordinary silver-ranker. He prepares to leave Rimaros rather than accept further royal interference.

Jason transfers the captured pagoda intruders to Liara rather than seeking revenge and arranges a decoy departure. A Shade body remains publicly associated with Soramir while the real Jason leaves under his new identity. The convoy includes Jason's team, Amos Pensinata and his nephew's team, Carlos Quilido's mobile prison-hospital, and several other allies. Their route favours populated regions and neglected contracts over speed. In a southern city, Arabelle Remore explains why Callum is so concerned about Melody Jane. Melody is Sophie's mother. She once concealed her family from the Order of the Reaper, entered the Cult of the Reaper, and was later forced to infiltrate the Order of Redeeming Light. Its purification turned her into an artificial zealot. Jason and Arabelle conclude that Sophie must make decisions for Melody while Melody cannot give informed consent. The revelation transforms Melody from a dangerous prisoner into an unresolved family responsibility.

Carlos continues stabilising Gibson Amouz, whose incomplete purification may offer clues for treating Melody and other converted victims. Amos begins intensive aura training with Jason, demanding precise control rather than raw force. The convoy reaches the ruins of Cartes, where a stolen astral space and a diamond-rank monster left a vast destruction zone. Jason registers as the cook John Miller to preserve his cover. He discovers a hidden Builder cult site and nearly exposes himself through an uncontrolled aura response, but the team presents him only as a sanctioned asset. Their work shows that the damaged region needs logistics more than additional combat teams, so the convoy moves on toward places where its abilities can make a material difference. Belinda's escalating thefts also force Humphrey to warn that her behaviour could endanger the whole team's reputation. The group leaves Cartes with Jason's identity intact, a clearer route, and Corinne Peskos's independent silver-rank team travelling alongside it.

Estella reports possible messenger activity near Yoresh, giving Jason both a threat to pursue and a possible source of astral knowledge for the unfinished Earth bridge. Farrah and Travis leave the convoy for Rimaros to develop long-distance communications and magitek weapons, making Jason's separation from Farrah immediate despite their residual soul bond. Corinne's team returns with Zara Rimaros, now using the adopted name Zara Noreen after abandoning the succession contest. Jason reacts with hostility because Zara once used his presumed death in a false engagement scheme. Arabelle challenges his surveillance and attempts to control Zara, and Jason agrees that Zara may remain under clinical supervision. Jason then enters Yoresh under the name John Miller with Estella. His covert investigation leads from an indebted pub owner to underground fight dens, where he enters a suppression-collar tournament and identifies an outworlder promoter. Taika, meanwhile, nears silver rank and resolves to support Jason without copying his self-destructive pursuit of power.

Jason's arena investigation shifts toward the promoter's elf aide, whose controlled aura suggests a concealed role. Amir Bahadir recognises Jason despite the cover and recruits his team into a worldwide search for a power that may cleanse monster-core effects from souls. Humphrey insists that any decision about such a discovery belongs to the team. The suspected aide is then confirmed as a messenger agent working with Lord Fal. Fal discovers Shade's surveillance and attacks Jason through the familiar link, but the encounter gives the Adventure Society a map of the agent's network. The Society warns that Yoresh's supply lines are vulnerable. Jason's team and Corinne's team are sent south after communications vanish across isolated settlements. The first silent town appears normal from a distance, yet Jason detects abnormal heat loss and identical behaviour among its residents. The teams suspect an externally controlled population positioned close to Yoresh and delay entering until they understand what is governing it.

Carlos identifies a likely heat-consuming parasite. Jason enters the silent settlement and discovers that its residents are corpses controlled by world-taker worms. His anger breaks his concealment, triggering a mass attack. The reunited team uses cold, cleansing, mobility, and wide-area powers to clear thousands of hosts while avoiding direct exposure. Jason and Clive locate a hidden messenger workshop beneath the town. A worm flood overwhelms Jason, but Gordon and Colin prevent the parasites from taking control. The silver-rank messenger operating the facility recognises Jason's body-soul nature and astral power, then becomes terrified of him. Jason defeats her, breaks her will through intimidation, and lets Colin kill and consume her. The wider infestation is confirmed as a deliberate messenger network extending through southern settlements. Although the immediate operator is dead, Jason's conduct troubles both him and his companions. He asks Shade to help keep him from crossing further into cruelty.

The team searches the messenger workshop and frees imprisoned adults, children, and adventurers who had been reserved for experimentation. Neil directs triage, while Sophie, Belinda, Humphrey, Arabelle, and Carlos help stabilise and relocate the survivors. Beneath the prison they find a world-taker worm matriarch and specialised worms. The team destroys the breeding stock rather than risk recreating the weapon. After consuming the matriarch, Colin can begin developing into a Voice of the Will, but doing so would keep the familiar dormant inside Jason's astral realm for an extended period. Jason converts his cloud structure into a hospital and refugee centre as the regional response expands. Disguised elite worm hosts attempt to infiltrate it, but the building traps them. The Healer then appears to Jason and explains that Purity sanctioned himself to create the sought-after core-cleansing relic. The gods will not intervene in the mortal struggle over it. The Healer also gives Jason a one-use core capable of granting true life to an astral construct.

Yoresh prepares for an expected messenger assault. Jason's cloud hospital becomes both a treatment centre for early worm extraction and a heavily defended refugee bunker, though its spirit-domain nature cuts priests off from direct contact with their gods. Inside the city, a messenger collaborator releases a Naga Genesis egg that had been hidden within the soul of the Valash fight promoter. A powerful Garuda hunter allows it to emerge in a form he can fight, and their diamond-rank battle devastates the city centre. Jason's team rescues civilians while Taika reaches silver rank during the evacuation. Messenger forces then surround Yoresh. Their plan is to use summons to thin the adaptive barrier, create temporary breaches, and strike civilian bunkers while the city's strongest defenders are occupied. Jason identifies the bunkers as the true targets. The refugees are sealed into the cloud defences, and the messengers move into position on every side of the city.

The siege begins as messenger summons pour through breaches above the bunkers. Jason's team defends the entertainment district from Onslow's flying shell, while Gareth Xandier leads civilian rescues nearer the centre. Corinne's team uses Zara's hurricane powers to set up large electrical attacks. Humphrey anchors the frontline, Sophie disrupts mobile threats, and Clive and Belinda combine ritual artillery with repeated resets. Jason attempts to spread afflictions through the horde, then shifts to tying down messenger defenders when they contain his chain. The invaders answer the adventurers' momentum with a coordinated aura assault. Jason's pyramid projects his own aura and heavy weapons across the vehicle district. A silver-rank messenger is sent to confront him and is dragged inside, where flight and aura advantages are restricted. Taika intercepts the intruder. His new Garuda authority disrupts the messenger's instincts, beginning a close fight within the shifting cloud corridors as gold-rank messengers prepare to force entry.

Taika defeats the trapped messenger and takes him alive, while the pyramid seals gold-rank intruders away from civilians. Across the entertainment district, messenger aura suppression begins turning the battle. Gordon constructs an alien ritual, and Jason opens his astral gate to power it despite the danger. The resulting projection displays Jason's soul across Yoresh and breaks the harmonic link between messenger auras. Adventurers regain the initiative, while messengers freeze, panic, or become enraged. Their leaders recognise Jason as evidence of an unprecedented route to astral-king power. A diamond-rank messenger moves to kill him, but Wraith intervenes outside normal time and leaves the messenger's corpse at Jason's feet. Jason harvests its life force and gains another resurrection state. Gold-rank enemies still converge on him. Onslow's shell is destroyed, scattering the team, and messenger isolation powers split several members into forced duels as the siege enters its final phase.

Terra June Castor traps Jason in a soul-shell duel that suppresses magic, familiars, items, and outside aid. Their close fight crashes into a civilian bunker. When Terra considers hostages, Jason discovers that his astral realm is inseparable from his soul and can partly resist the suppression. He forces access to Terra's soul, takes control of the duel, and removes both her astral-king brand and the seal holding her at silver rank. Terra survives unconscious. A gold-rank messenger commander then asks Jason for asylum, arguing that only an astral king can shelter the defectors. Jason provisionally accepts and takes the group into his realm. Over the following weeks he helps consenting messengers replace their ruler's marks with their own, refusing to own or coerce them. One dies when the former astral king removes its mark. Yoresh survives and the raid ends in withdrawal. The defectors reveal a deeper campaign around a natural array, a subterranean city, Builder cultists, and an unknown buried objective. Jason expects pressure to lead the next expedition.

characters.description: A displaced man who wakes in the Vane estate maze without an explanation for his arrival. An intuitive interface gives him survival tools, quests, and an inventory, which already contains a mysterious World Phoenix token.
characters.name: Jason Asano

characters.name: Unconscious Ritualist

characters.name: Landemere Vane

characters.description: Landemere Vane's mother and a leader of the blood cult holding Jason and four adventurers for sacrifice. She suspects Jason killed her son and orders him retained for the coming blood feast.
characters.name: Cressida Vane

characters.description: A captive adventurer imprisoned with Jason at the Vane estate. He remains composed enough to explain how spirit coins can temporarily enhance physical and magical attributes, helping Jason formulate an escape.
characters.name: Rufus Remore

characters.description: An exceptionally large, lion-headed prisoner held for the blood feast. Even with a suppression collar blocking his essence abilities, his natural strength makes him a formidable prospective ally.
characters.name: Gary

characters.description: An elf captive held with Rufus, Gary, and another adventurer as an intended sacrifice in the Vane blood feast.
characters.name: Anisa

characters.description: The blood cult's high priest. He intervenes during the prisoners' escape and uses binding magic to immobilize Rufus and Gary.
characters.name: Darryl Caruthers

characters.name: Farrah

characters.name: Sanguine Horror

characters.name: Hiram

characters.name: Colin

characters.name: Old City Alchemist

characters.name: Gareth Xandier

characters.description: The Geller family's son, awaiting final training and an Adventure Society field assessment that Rufus agrees to conduct.
characters.name: Humphrey Geller

characters.name: Stash

characters.description: An acolyte of the Church of Knowledge assigned to assist with Jason's Adventure Society assessment.
characters.name: Gabrielle Pellin

characters.name: Lucian Lamprey

characters.description: Lucian Lamprey's elf deputy and the official who manages much of the Greenstone Magic Society's daily operation.
characters.name: Pochard Finn

characters.description: A Magic Society investigator assigned to examine the anomalous spirit coins bearing Jason's identifying inscription. He considers the possibility that an essence ability, rather than an illegal coin farm, created them.
characters.name: Clive Standish

characters.description: A former pit fighter known as Nightingale. Clarissa Ventress forces her back into the cage to provoke another interested party, despite Sophie's earlier release from fighting.
characters.name: Sophie

characters.name: Belinda

characters.name: Clarissa Ventress

characters.name: Goddess of Knowledge

characters.description: Humphrey Geller's silver-rank mother and an overseer of the family's training estate. She introduces Jason to the mirage chamber while Rufus begins correcting Humphrey's hesitation under pressure.
characters.name: Danielle Geller

characters.name: Emir

characters.name: Gabriel Remore

characters.name: Cole Silva

characters.name: Sophie Wexler

characters.name: Thalia Mercer

characters.name: Cassandra Mercer

characters.name: Vincent Trenslow

characters.name: Thadwick Mercer

characters.name: Jory

characters.name: Elspeth Arella

characters.name: Rick Geller

characters.name: Onslow

characters.name: Phoebe Geller

characters.name: Beth Cavendish

characters.name: Jory Tillman

characters.name: Dean Tuckle

characters.name: Dominion
